source: Try the trick (double, add four, divide by two, subtract the

items.question: Try the trick (double, add four, divide by two, subtract the start) with 5 and with 11, then explain with a letter-number why it always ends on 2.
steps: Start with 5: 5 × 2 = 10, then 10 + 4 = 14, then 14 ÷ 2 = 7, then 7 − 5 = 2.
Start with x: double it to get 2x, add four to get 2x + 4, divide by 2 to get x + 2.
Subtract the start: x + 2 − x leaves 2, whatever x is.
items.answer: It always ends on 2, because the starting number cancels out

videos.answer: It always ends on 2, because the starting number cancels out

source: Change the trick so it always ends on 3, then on 5. Then che

items.question: Change the trick so it always ends on 3, then on 5. Then check this longer trick: think of a number, multiply by 3, add 12, divide by 3, subtract the number.
steps: Add six instead of four: 2x + 6, divided by 2 is x + 3, and x + 3 − x leaves 3.
Add ten instead: 2x + 10, divided by 2 is x + 5, and subtracting x leaves 5.
Longer trick with x: 3x, then 3x + 12, then x + 4, then x + 4 − x leaves 4.
items.answer: Add 6 for a final 3, add 10 for a final 5; the longer trick always ends on 4

videos.answer: Add 6 for a final 3, add 10 for a final 5; the longer trick always ends on 4

source: Mukta thinks of 26 January and follows the steps. Show that

items.question: Mukta thinks of 26 January and follows the steps. Show that she gets 291, and how Shubham reads the date back from 291.
steps: Add the day: 265 + 26 = 291.
With letters the answer is always 100M + 165 + D.
Subtract 165: 291 − 165 = 126, which is 100M + D.
The last two digits, 26, are the day and the digit before them, 1, is the month.
items.answer: 26 January: the answer minus 165 shows the month followed by the two digit day

videos.answer: 26 January: the answer minus 165 shows the month followed by the two digit day

source: Mukta reports 1390. Which date did she think of? Check by ru

items.question: Mukta reports 1390. Which date did she think of? Check by running the trick forward.
steps: The last two digits give the day, 25. The digits before them give the month, 12.
Add the day: 1365 + 25 = 1390. It matches.
items.answer: 25 December

videos.answer: 25 December

source: New steps: multiply the month by 10, add 7, multiply by 10,

items.question: New steps: multiply the month by 10, add 7, multiply by 10, add the day. What do you subtract to read the date? A friend reports 1295.
steps: With letters: 10M, then 10M + 7, then 100M + 70, then 100M + 70 + D.
So subtract 70 to leave 100M + D.
For the friend: 1295 − 70 = 1225, so month 12 and day 25.
items.answer: Subtract 70; the friend chose 25 December

videos.answer: Subtract 70; the friend chose 25 December

source: Think of a Number tricks: find the dates

items.question: Find the dates if the final answers of the date trick are the following: (i) 1269 (ii) 394 (iii) 296.
steps: (i) 1269 − 165 = 1104: the day is 04 and the month is 11, so 4 November.
(ii) 394 − 165 = 229: the day is 29 and the month is 2, so 29 February, a leap year date.
(iii) 296 − 165 = 131: the day is 31 and the month is 1, so 31 January.
items.answer: (i) 4 November (ii) 29 February (iii) 31 January

videos.answer: (i) 4 November (ii) 29 February (iii) 31 January

source: Fill the pyramids with bottom rows 6, 2 and 3, 4, 3 and 5, 4

items.question: Fill the pyramids with bottom rows 6, 2 and 3, 4, 3 and 5, 4, 5, 0.
steps: Bottom row 6, 2: the top is 6 + 2 = 8.
Bottom row 3, 4, 3: the middle row is 3 + 4 = 7 and 4 + 3 = 7, and the top is 7 + 7 = 14.
Bottom row 5, 4, 5, 0: the next row is 5 + 4 = 9, 4 + 5 = 9 and 5 + 0 = 5.
Then 9 + 9 = 18 and 9 + 5 = 14, and the top is 18 + 14 = 32.
items.answer: Tops 8, 14 and 32

videos.answer: Tops 8, 14 and 32

source: A pyramid has top 10, middle row 4 and a blank, and bottom r

items.question: A pyramid has top 10, middle row 4 and a blank, and bottom row 1 and two blanks. Fill it.
steps: The middle blank is 10 − 4 = 6.
Below the 4 sit 1 and a blank, so that blank is 4 − 1 = 3.
Below the 6 sit 3 and the last blank, so it is 6 − 3 = 3.
items.answer: Middle row 4, 6; bottom row 1, 3, 3

videos.answer: Middle row 4, 6; bottom row 1, 3, 3

source: Fill the pyramid with top 60 and bottom row 12, a blank, 8.

items.question: Fill the pyramid with top 60 and bottom row 12, a blank, 8.
steps: Call the middle row a and b and the bottom blank c.
The rule gives a + b = 60, a = 12 + c and b = c + 8.
Then 2c = 40, so c is 20, a is 32 and b is 28.
items.answer: Middle row 32, 28; bottom row 12, 20, 8

videos.answer: Middle row 32, 28; bottom row 12, 20, 8

source: Fill the four row pyramid with top 50, second row a blank an

items.question: Fill the four row pyramid with top 50, second row a blank and 22, and bottom row 4, a blank, 6, a blank.
steps: Call the bottom blanks p and q: the bottom row is 4, p, 6, q.
Third row: 4 + p, p + 6, 6 + q. The 22 is (p + 6) + (6 + q), so p + q + 12 = 22 and p + q = 10.
The top is (4 + p) + 2(p + 6) + (6 + q), which is 3p + q + 22, so 3p + q + 22 = 50 and 3p + q = 28.
Take p + q = 10 away from 3p + q = 28: that leaves 2p = 18, so p is 9 and q is 1.
Third row 13, 15, 7; second row 28, 22; check 28 + 22 = 50.
items.answer: Bottom row 4, 9, 6, 1; third row 13, 15, 7; second row 28, 22

videos.answer: Bottom row 4, 9, 6, 1; third row 13, 15, 7; second row 28, 22

source: Fill the pyramid with second row 40 and a blank, third row e

items.question: Fill the pyramid with second row 40 and a blank, third row ending in 9, and bottom row 5, a blank, 7, a blank. Then fill the pyramid with top 35, third row ending in 7, and bottom row 3, 5, two blanks.
steps: Second pyramid: the last bottom box is 9 − 7 = 2. Call the other blank p.
The 40 is (5 + p) + (p + 7), so 2p + 12 = 40 and p is 14. Third row 19, 21, 9; second row 40, 30; top 40 + 30 = 70.
Third pyramid: call the bottom blanks r and s, so r + s = 7 from the 7 above them.
The top is 3 + 3 × 5 + 3r + s, so 18 + 3r + s = 35 and 3r + s = 17. With r + s = 7, 2r = 10, so r is 5 and s is 2.
Third row 8, 10, 7; second row 18, 17; check 18 + 17 = 35.
items.answer: First: bottom 5, 14, 7, 2 and top 70. Second: bottom 3, 5, 5, 2 with rows 8, 10, 7 and 18, 17

videos.answer: First: bottom 5, 14, 7, 2 and top 70. Second: bottom 3, 5, 5, 2 with rows 8, 10, 7 and 18, 17

source: Write the top of a three row pyramid with bottom row a, b, c

items.question: Write the top of a three row pyramid with bottom row a, b, c. Use it for the bottom row 1, 9, 4.
steps: The middle row is a + b and b + c.
The top is (a + b) + (b + c), which is a + 2b + c.
Building it gives 10, 13 and then 23, the same top.
items.answer: The top is a + 2b + c; for 1, 9, 4 it is 23

videos.answer: The top is a + 2b + c; for 1, 9, 4 it is 23

items.question: Write an expression for the topmost row of a pyramid with 4 rows in terms of the values in the bottom row.
steps: Bottom row a, b, c, d. The next row is a + b, b + c, c + d.
The row above that is a + 2b + c and b + 2c + d.
The top is (a + 2b + c) + (b + 2c + d), which is a + 3b + 3c + d.
items.answer: a + 3b + 3c + d

source: Figure it Out (number pyramids, question 4)

items.question: Recall the Virahanka-Fibonacci number sequence 1, 2, 3, 5, ... where each number is the sum of the two numbers before it. If the first three Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers are written in the bottom row of a number pyramid with three rows, fill in the rest of the pyramid. What numbers appear in the grid? What is the number at the top? Are they all Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers?
steps: The bottom row is 1, 2, 3.
The middle row is 1 + 2 = 3 and 2 + 3 = 5.
The top is 3 + 5 = 8.
The sequence goes 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, so every number in the grid is in it.
items.answer: The grid holds 1, 2, 3, 3, 5 and 8; the top is 8; all are Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers

videos.answer: The grid holds 1, 2, 3, 3, 5 and 8; the top is 8; all are Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers

source: Figure it Out (number pyramids, question 5)

items.question: What can you say about the numbers in the pyramid and the number at the top in the following cases? (i) The first four Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers are written in the bottom row of a four row pyramid. (ii) The first 29 Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers are written in the bottom row of a 29 row pyramid.
steps: (i) Bottom row 1, 2, 3, 5. Next row 3, 5, 8. Next row 8, 13. Top 8 + 13 = 21.
All of them are Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers, and the top 21 is the 7th number of 1, 2, 3, 5, ...
Two neighbours in the sequence add to the number two places further on, so every row is again a run of Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers, moved two places along.
(ii) Each row moves two places along, so after 28 steps up the single top box is the 57th number of the sequence.
items.answer: (i) All are Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers and the top is 21 (ii) All are Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers and the top is the 57th number of the sequence

videos.answer: (i) All are Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers and the top is 21 (ii) All are Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers and the top is the 57th number of the sequence

source: Figure it Out (number pyramids, question 6)

items.question: If the bottom row of an n row pyramid contains the first n Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers, what can we say about the numbers in the pyramid? What can we say about the number at the top?
steps: Two neighbours of the sequence add to the number two places further on.
So each row is a run of Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers, starting two places further along than the row below.
The bottom row starts at the 1st number, so the top row, n − 1 steps up, is the number at place 1 + 2(n − 1), which is the (2n − 1)th number.
Check: n = 3 gives the 5th number, 8; n = 4 gives the 7th number, 21.
items.answer: Every number in the pyramid is a Virahanka-Fibonacci number, and the top is the (2n − 1)th number of the sequence

videos.answer: Every number in the pyramid is a Virahanka-Fibonacci number, and the top is the (2n − 1)th number of the sequence

source: A friend picks a 2 by 2 block from a calendar page and says

items.question: A friend picks a 2 by 2 block from a calendar page and says the sum is 36. Find the block. Check the trick on the block 6, 7, 13, 14 too.
steps: Write the block as a, a + 1, a + 7, a + 8. The sum is 4a + 16.
So 4a + 16 = 36, which gives 4a = 20 and a is 5.
items.answer: The block is 5, 6, 12, 13

videos.answer: The block is 5, 6, 12, 13

source: A friend picks three dates one below the other on a calendar

items.question: A friend picks three dates one below the other on a calendar page and says their sum is 51. Find the dates.
steps: Call the top date a. The dates below it are a + 7 and a + 14.
The sum is a + (a + 7) + (a + 14), which is 3a + 21.
So 3a + 21 = 51, which gives 3a = 30 and a is 10.
The dates are 10, 17 and 24. Check: 10 + 17 + 24 = 51.

source: In a grid, three squares make 27 and two circles with a squa

items.question: In a grid, three squares make 27 and two circles with a square make 19. Find the square and the circle.
steps: Three equal squares make 27, so one square is 27 ÷ 3 = 9.
Two circles and a square make 19, so two circles make 19 − 9 = 10.
One circle is 10 ÷ 2 = 5.
items.answer: Square 9, circle 5

videos.answer: Square 9, circle 5

source: Fun with Grids: fill the algebra grids

items.question: In the following grids, find the values of the shapes and fill in the empty squares. Grid 1: square, square, circle make 27; circle, circle, square make 21; circle, square, circle make a blank. Grid 2: circle, diamond, diamond make 18; diamond, circle, circle make 15; diamond, circle, circle make a blank; the last row is blank under every column.
steps: Grid 1: two squares and a circle make 27, two circles and a square make 21.
Adding both rows, three squares and three circles make 48, so a square and a circle make 16.
Take that from the first row: one square is 27 − 16 = 11, so a circle is 5. The last row is 5 + 11 + 5 = 21.
Grid 2: a circle and two diamonds make 18, two circles and a diamond make 15, so a circle and a diamond make 33 ÷ 3 = 11.
One diamond is 18 − 11 = 7 and a circle is 4. The third row is 7 + 4 + 4 = 15.
Read the last row as column sums: 4 + 7 + 7 = 18, 7 + 4 + 4 = 15, 7 + 4 + 4 = 15, and the corner is 18 + 15 + 15 = 48.
items.answer: Grid 1: square 11, circle 5, last row 21. Grid 2: circle 4, diamond 7, third row 15, column sums 18, 15, 15 and 48 in the corner

videos.answer: Grid 1: square 11, circle 5, last row 21. Grid 2: circle 4, diamond 7, third row 15, column sums 18, 15, 15 and 48 in the corner

source: Place the digits 2, 3 and 5 to make the largest two digit by

items.question: Place the digits 2, 3 and 5 to make the largest two digit by one digit product.
steps: In each pair with the same multiplier keep the larger: 53 × 2, 52 × 3 and 32 × 5.
By place value: 32 × 5 = 150 + 10 and 52 × 3 = 150 + 6, so 32 × 5 wins.
items.answer: 32 × 5 = 160 is the largest product

videos.answer: 32 × 5 = 160 is the largest product

source: Show that qp × r is the largest product for digits p < q < r

items.question: Show that qp × r is the largest product for digits p < q < r, and check it with the digits 4, 6 and 8.
steps: Keep the larger of each pair: rq × p, rp × q and qp × r.
Expand: rp × q is 10 × r × q plus p × q, and rq × p is 10 × r × p plus q × p. The ones parts match and q > p, so rp × q is bigger.
Expand: qp × r is 10 × q × r plus p × r, and rp × q is 10 × r × q plus p × q.
The tens parts match and p × r is bigger than p × q, so qp × r is the largest.
items.answer: qp × r is always the largest; for 4, 6 and 8 it is 64 × 8 = 512

videos.answer: qp × r is always the largest; for 4, 6 and 8 it is 64 × 8 = 512

source: Shubham picks 47. Follow Mukta's trick, then show with lette

items.question: Shubham picks 47. Follow Mukta's trick, then show with letters why 9 always divides the difference.
steps: Reverse 47 to get 74. The difference is 74 − 47 = 27, and 27 ÷ 9 = 3 with no remainder.
Write the number as 10a + b and the reverse as 10b + a, with b larger than a.
The difference is 10b + a − 10a − b, which is 9b − 9a, or 9 times (b − a).
For 47 the digit difference is 7 − 4 = 3, which is the quotient.
items.answer: The difference is always 9 times the difference of the digits

videos.answer: The difference is always 9 times the difference of the digits

source: Take 83, whose first digit is bigger. Follow the trick and s

items.question: Take 83, whose first digit is bigger. Follow the trick and show what happens with letters when a > b.
steps: Reverse 83 to get 38. The difference is 83 − 38 = 45, and 45 ÷ 9 = 5.
With a > b, subtract the reverse from the number: 10a + b − 10b − a.
That is 9a − 9b, which is 9 times (a − b).
For 83, the digit difference is 8 − 3 = 5, which is the quotient again.
items.answer: The difference is 9 times (a − b), so 9 still divides it

videos.answer: The difference is 9 times (a − b), so 9 still divides it

source: Take 352, reverse it to 253 and subtract. Show with letters

items.question: Take 352, reverse it to 253 and subtract. Show with letters why 99 always divides the difference of a three digit number and its reverse.
steps: Write abc as 100a + 10b + c and its reverse as 100c + 10b + a, with a larger than c.
The difference is 100a + c − 100c − a, the tens cancel, which is 99a − 99c.
That is 99 times (a − c), so 99 always divides it. For 352, the difference of the outer digits is 3 − 2 = 1.
items.answer: The difference is 99 times the difference of the first and last digits

videos.answer: The difference is 99 times the difference of the first and last digits

source: Figure it Out (divisibility tricks, question 1)

items.question: In the trick given above, what is the quotient when you divide by 9? Is there a relationship between the two numbers and the quotient?
steps: The difference is 9 times the difference of the digits.
So dividing by 9 leaves the difference of the two digits.
items.answer: The quotient is the difference between the two digits of the number

videos.answer: The quotient is the difference between the two digits of the number

source: Figure it Out (divisibility tricks, question 2)

items.question: In the trick given above, instead of finding the difference of the two 2 digit numbers, find their sum. What will happen? For example: 31 + 13 = 44, 28 + 82 = 110, 12 + 21 = 33. Observe that all these numbers are divisible by 11. Is this always true? Can we justify this claim using algebra?
steps: The number is 10a + b and the reverse is 10b + a.
The sum is 11a + 11b, which is 11 times (a + b).
So the sum is always divisible by 11, and the quotient is the digit sum: 44 ÷ 11 = 4 and 3 + 1 = 4.
items.answer: Yes, always: the sum is 11 times the sum of the digits

videos.answer: Yes, always: the sum is 11 times the sum of the digits

source: Figure it Out (divisibility tricks, question 3)

items.question: Consider any 3 digit number, say abc (100a + 10b + c). Make two other 3 digit numbers from these digits by cycling these digits around, yielding bca and cab. Now add the three numbers. Using algebra, justify that the sum is always divisible by 37. Will it also always be divisible by 3? (Hint: Look at some multiples of 37.)
steps: abc is 100a + 10b + c, bca is 100b + 10c + a and cab is 100c + 10a + b.
Each digit appears once as hundreds, once as tens and once as ones, so the sum is 111a + 111b + 111c.
That is 111 times (a + b + c), and 111 = 3 × 37.
items.answer: The sum is 111 times (a + b + c); since 111 = 3 × 37 it is always divisible by 37 and by 3

videos.answer: The sum is 111 times (a + b + c); since 111 = 3 × 37 it is always divisible by 37 and by 3

source: Figure it Out (divisibility tricks, question 4)

items.question: Consider any 3 digit number, say abc. Make it a 6 digit number by repeating the digits, that is abcabc. Divide this number by 7, then by 11, and finally by 13. What do you get? Try this with other numbers. Figure out why it works. (Hint: Multiply 7, 11 and 13.)
steps: Repeating the digits means abc × 1000 + abc, which is abc × 1001.
And 7 × 11 × 13 = 1001, so dividing by 7, 11 and 13 divides by 1001.
items.answer: You get back the original 3 digit number, because abcabc is abc × 1001 and 1001 = 7 × 11 × 13

videos.answer: You get back the original 3 digit number, because abcabc is abc × 1001 and 1001 = 7 × 11 × 13

source: A stand has 20 cycles, some bicycles and some tricycles, wit

items.question: A stand has 20 cycles, some bicycles and some tricycles, with 46 wheels in all. How many of each?
steps: Let t be the number of tricycles, so there are 20 − t bicycles.
Wheels: 3t + 2(20 − t) = 46, so t + 40 = 46 and t is 6.
There are 6 tricycles and 14 bicycles. Check: 3 × 6 + 2 × 14 = 18 + 28 = 46.
Without letters: 20 bicycles would have 40 wheels; each tricycle adds 1 more, and 46 − 40 = 6.
items.answer: 6 tricycles and 14 bicycles

videos.answer: 6 tricycles and 14 bicycles

source: Asha has some stickers. She doubles them and gives away 5, t

items.question: Asha has some stickers. She doubles them and gives away 5, then doubles again and gives away 5. She has 13 left. How many did she start with?
steps: Let x be the start. After round one she has 2x − 5.
After round two she has 2(2x − 5) − 5, which is 4x − 15.
So 4x − 15 = 13, which gives 4x = 28 and x is 7.
items.answer: She started with 7 stickers

videos.answer: She started with 7 stickers

items.question: A lemonade stall pays rent of ₹200 a day, and each glass costs ₹5 to make. If 60 glasses are sold, what price per glass gives a profit of ₹400?
steps: Let the price be p rupees. Income is 60p.
Costs: rent 200 and making 60 × 5 = 300.
items.answer: ₹15 per glass

videos.answer: ₹15 per glass

source: Figure it Out (divisibility tricks, question 5)

items.question: There are 3 shrines, each with a magical pond in the front. If anyone dips flowers into these magical ponds, the number of flowers doubles. A person has some flowers. He dips them all in the first pond and then places some flowers in shrine 1. Next, he dips the remaining flowers in the second pond and places some flowers in shrine 2. Finally, he dips the remaining flowers in the third pond and then places them all in shrine 3. If he placed an equal number of flowers in each shrine, how many flowers did he start with? How many flowers did he place in each shrine?
steps: Let x be the start and k the flowers placed in each shrine.
After the first pond and shrine: 2x − k. After the second: 2(2x − k) − k, which is 4x − 3k.
The third pond doubles it to 8x − 6k, and all of it goes into shrine 3, so 8x − 6k = k and 8x = 7k.
The smallest whole numbers are x = 7 and k = 8. Check: 14 − 8 = 6, then 12 − 8 = 4, then 8.
Any multiple also works, such as 14 flowers with 16 in each shrine.
items.answer: He started with 7 flowers and placed 8 in each shrine (or any multiple, like 14 and 16)

videos.answer: He started with 7 flowers and placed 8 in each shrine (or any multiple, like 14 and 16)

source: Figure it Out (divisibility tricks, question 6)

items.question: A farm has some horses and hens. The total number of heads of these animals is 55 and the total number of legs is 150. How many horses and how many hens are on the farm? Can you solve this without letter-numbers? (Hint: If all the 55 animals were hens, then how many legs would there be? Using the difference between this number and 150, can you find the number of horses?)
steps: Let h be the horses, so there are 55 − h hens.
Without letters: 55 hens would have 110 legs. 150 − 110 = 40 legs are extra, and each horse adds 2, so 40 ÷ 2 = 20 horses.
items.answer: 20 horses and 35 hens

videos.answer: 20 horses and 35 hens

source: Figure it Out (divisibility tricks, question 7)

items.question: A mother is 5 times her daughter's age. In 6 years' time, the mother will be 3 times her daughter's age. How old is the daughter now?
steps: Let the daughter be d years old, so the mother is 5d.
In 6 years: 5d + 6 = 3(d + 6), which is 3d + 18.
So 2d = 12 and d is 6.
Check: the mother is 30 now; in 6 years 36 = 3 × 12.
items.answer: The daughter is 6 years old

videos.answer: The daughter is 6 years old

source: Figure it Out (divisibility tricks, question 8)

items.question: Two friends, Gauri and Naina, are cowherds. One day, they pass each other on the road with their cows. Gauri says to Naina, "You have twice as many cows as I do". Naina says, "That's true, but if I gave you three of my cows, we would each have the same number of cows". How many cows do Gauri and Naina have?
steps: Let Gauri have g cows, so Naina has 2g.
If Naina gives 3: 2g − 3 = g + 3, so g is 6.
Naina has 12. Check: 12 − 3 = 9 and 6 + 3 = 9.
items.answer: Gauri has 6 cows and Naina has 12

videos.answer: Gauri has 6 cows and Naina has 12

source: Figure it Out (divisibility tricks, question 9)

items.question: I run a small dosa cart and my expenses are as follows: rent for the dosa cart is ₹5000 per day; the cost of making one dosa (including all the ingredients and fuel) is ₹10. (i) If I can sell 100 dosas a day, what should be the selling price of my dosa to make a profit of ₹2000? (ii) If my customers are willing to pay only ₹50 for a dosa, how many dosas should I aim to sell in a day to make a profit of ₹2000?
steps: (i) Let the price be p. Income 100p; costs 5000 + 100 × 10 = 6000.
(ii) Let n dosas be sold. Each earns 50 − 10 = 40 after its own cost.
items.answer: (i) ₹80 per dosa (ii) 175 dosas a day

videos.answer: (i) ₹80 per dosa (ii) 175 dosas a day

source: Figure it Out (divisibility tricks, question 10)

items.question: Evaluate the following sequence of fractions: 1 ÷ 3, (1 + 3) ÷ (5 + 7), (1 + 3 + 5) ÷ (7 + 9 + 11). What do you observe? Can you explain why this happens? (Hint: Recall what you know about the sum of the first n odd numbers.)
steps: (1 + 3) ÷ (5 + 7) = 4 ÷ 12, which is one third.
(1 + 3 + 5) ÷ (7 + 9 + 11) = 9 ÷ 27, which is one third again.
The first n odd numbers add up to n × n, and the first 2n odd numbers add up to 4 × n × n.
So the next n odd numbers add up to 4 × n × n minus n × n, which is 3 × n × n, three times the top.
items.answer: Every fraction equals one third, because the bottom sum is always three times the top sum

items.question: Karim and the Genie. Each time Karim goes around the banyan tree, the coins in his pocket double, and then he gives the genie 8 coins. After the third round the coins doubled, and he was left with only 8 coins, exactly the number he owed the genie. (i) How many coins did Karim initially have? (ii) For what cost per round should Karim agree to the deal, if he wants to increase the number of coins he has? (iii) Through its magical powers, the genie knows the number of coins that Karim has. How should the genie set the cost per round so that it gets all of Karim's coins?
steps: (i) Let x be the start. After one round 2x − 8, after two rounds 4x − 24.
The third doubling gives 8x − 48, which is 8, so 8x = 56 and x is 7.
Check: 7, then 14 − 8 = 6, then 12 − 8 = 4, then 8, all given to the genie.
(ii) With cost c, one round turns x into 2x − c, which is more than x only when c is less than x. So Karim should agree only if the cost is less than the coins he starts with, here fewer than 7.
(iii) After three rounds he has 8x − 7c. For this to be 0, the genie sets c to 8x ÷ 7. For 7 coins that is 8 per round, exactly the genie's trick.
items.answer: (i) 7 coins (ii) a cost per round less than his coins, fewer than 7 (iii) 8 ÷ 7 of his starting coins per round, which is 8 when he starts with 7
